purpose: Independent practice of A7.1 — predicting the next element and creating an AB pattern. Used as a Lesson 1 consolidation artifact and as evidence for the diagnostic checklist.
student_learning_goal: I can spot a pattern and say what comes next.

parts.student_instructions: Bea and Finn are leading the parade. Look at the pattern. Draw or sticker the animal that comes next.
parts.visual_layout: Horizontal parade strip centred on the page, 5 cells wide, each cell ~1.2in square. Cells 1–4 are filled with the animal icons in the order Bea, Finn, Bea, Finn. Cell 5 has a dashed outline (no fill) to signal the empty space the student fills in. Footprints decorate the strip beneath the cells, suggesting a parade route. To the left of the strip, a small reference key shows just the Bea and Finn icons with their names underneath, so children using markers (not stickers) know how to draw them.

parts.student_instructions: Two animals are missing from this parade. Look carefully at the pattern. Draw or sticker the missing animals in the empty boxes.
parts.visual_layout: Horizontal parade strip centred on the page, 7 cells wide, each cell ~1in square (slightly smaller than Part 1 to fit). Cells 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 are filled with: Bea, Finn, Bea, Bea, Finn (the pattern continuing). Cell 4 (middle, missing) and cell 7 (end, missing) have dashed outlines. Footprints beneath the strip as in Part 1. To the left, a thin small reference key showing Bea and Finn again.

parts.answer_key: Any valid AB pattern using exactly two of the four animals. A response is correct if: (a) cells 1, 3, 5 contain the same animal; (b) cells 2, 4 contain the same animal; (c) cells 1 and 2 contain different animals. Examples: Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn-Bea; Bibi-Moss-Bibi-Moss-Bibi; Finn-Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn; Moss-Bea-Moss-Bea-Moss. Accept any valid combination.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over and build another parade with two different animals! Can you make a longer one with all four animals?
teacher_notes: This worksheet is a Lesson 1 consolidation artifact. Hand it out at the end of the Action phase, after the partner-build activity. Most children should complete Parts 1 and 2 independently if they were successful at the partner activity. For Part 3, look for: (a) the child used exactly two different animals, and (b) the pattern alternates correctly. Use Part 3 as evidence for the diagnostic checklist column 'Creates pattern (independent)'. Children who struggle with Part 3 likely need a re-loop on Lesson 1 before moving to Lesson 2.
